lessons.learning_objective: Describe and quantify association between two variables

lessons.key_concepts: Equation, slope and intercept interpretation, coefficient of determination r squared

lessons.common_misconceptions: Students interpret slope and intercept without context

lessons.key_concepts: Residual equals observed minus predicted, positive residual means the model underpredicts, residual plots, curvature signals a nonlinear form
lessons.key_vocabulary: residual, residual plot, predicted value
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students miss when residual patterns suggest nonlinearity
lessons.real_world_hook: Improving forecast models

units.unit_title: AP exam practice (not a College Board CED unit)

lessons.learning_objective: Describe the format of the AP Statistics exam and practice each section under exam conditions
lessons.key_concepts: The exam is 3 hours and fully digital in the Bluebook app starting May 2027; Section I is 42 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes, worth 50% of the score, with four answer choices each; Section II is 4 free-response questions in 90 minutes, worth 50%, each worth 10 points and 12.5%; Question 1 focuses on formulating questions and collecting data, Question 2 on analyzing data and interpreting results, Question 3 is an inference question (hypothesis test or confidence interval), and Question 4 combines collecting data, analyzing data, and interpreting results; a graphing calculator with statistical capabilities is expected on both sections; formulas and tables are provided for both sections; multiple-choice weighting is Unit 1 20-30%, Unit 2 15-25%, Unit 3 15-25%, Unit 4 10-20%, Unit 5 10-20%
lessons.key_vocabulary: multiple choice, free response, Bluebook, formula sheet, statistical practices
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students memorize the standard error formula for a proportion and waste time rewriting it from memory instead of using the provided formula sheet, then copy it incorrectly
lessons.real_world_hook: Running a full dress rehearsal before opening night

lessons.learning_objective: Write complete, in-context free-response answers and pace the 90-minute free-response section
lessons.key_concepts: About 22 minutes per free-response question; read all four questions first; for inference, name the procedure, state hypotheses with parameters defined, check conditions, show the test statistic or interval, and conclude in context with a comparison to alpha; every answer must refer to the context of the problem; use calculator output only with the name of the procedure and the values that went into it; attempt every part since parts are scored separately
lessons.key_vocabulary: context, conditions, conclusion, pacing, calculator speak
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write only '1-PropZTest, p = 0.03, reject H0' with no hypotheses, conditions, or conclusion in context, and lose most of the credit for a correct calculation
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a lab report that a skeptical reviewer can check line by line

lessons.learning_objective: Calculate earnings from hourly wages, overtime, salary, and commission and compare job offers on an annual and hourly basis
lessons.key_concepts: Gross pay = hours x rate; federal law generally requires time-and-a-half (1.5 x rate) for nonexempt workers' hours over 40 in a workweek; annual salary from hourly (rate x hours per week x weeks per year, often about 2,080 hours for full time); commission as a percent of sales; comparing offers that include benefits, not just pay
lessons.key_vocabulary: gross pay, hourly wage, salary, overtime, time-and-a-half, commission, benefits
lessons.common_misconceptions: Calculates 45 hours at $16/hour with overtime as 45 x 1.5 x 16 = $1,080, paying all hours at overtime instead of 40 x 16 + 5 x 24 = $760; compares a $40,000 salary with a $20/hour job without converting either to the same unit
lessons.real_world_hook: Choosing between a $19/hour retail job and a $42,000 salaried job with health insurance

lessons.lesson_title: Gross vs net pay and paycheck withholding
lessons.learning_objective: Read a pay stub, distinguish gross from net pay, and calculate common deductions such as income tax withholding and FICA taxes
lessons.key_concepts: Gross pay is earnings before deductions; net pay (take-home) is after deductions; federal income tax withholding based on the W-4; FICA = Social Security plus Medicare, withheld as percentages of wages; state and local income tax in some states; pre-tax deductions (retirement contributions, health insurance) lower taxable income; progressive tax brackets: each rate applies only to income within that bracket
lessons.key_vocabulary: gross pay, net pay, pay stub, withholding, W-4, FICA, Social Security, Medicare, deduction, tax bracket
lessons.common_misconceptions: Believes a raise that moves you into a higher tax bracket can lower your take-home pay because the higher rate applies to all income; budgets with gross pay instead of net pay
lessons.real_world_hook: A teen's first paycheck says $600 gross but only about $520 hits the bank account; trace where the rest went

lessons.lesson_title: Percents in everyday spending: discounts, tax, and tips
lessons.learning_objective: Apply percents to compute sales tax, discounts, tips, markups, and percent change, and compare unit prices
lessons.key_concepts: Price after discount = price x (1 - d); price with tax = price x (1 + t); successive discounts multiply; tip on the pre-tax or post-tax amount; percent change; unit price comparison; percent of income going to each category
lessons.key_vocabulary: percent, discount, sales tax, markup, tip, unit price, percent change
lessons.common_misconceptions: Takes 25% off and then adds 8% tax by computing 25% - 8% = 17% off; thinks the larger package is always the better deal without comparing unit prices
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a $45 pair of shoes at 30% off with a $38 pair at 15% off, after 7% sales tax

lessons.learning_objective: Create a monthly budget from net income that separates fixed and variable expenses and needs and wants, and adjust it to meet a savings goal
lessons.key_concepts: Income minus expenses = savings or shortfall; fixed (rent, phone plan) vs variable (food, gas) expenses; needs vs wants; percentage guidelines such as 50/30/20 (needs/wants/savings) as a starting point, not a rule; emergency fund; tracking spending; converting weekly or annual amounts to monthly; inequalities to model staying within a budget
lessons.key_vocabulary: budget, income, fixed expense, variable expense, need, want, emergency fund, surplus, deficit
lessons.common_misconceptions: Builds the budget from gross income; treats an annual expense like car insurance as if it does not exist because it is not paid monthly
lessons.real_world_hook: Planning a first-apartment budget on $2,400 a month take-home pay, including rent, groceries, transportation, and savings

lessons.learning_objective: Compare checking and savings accounts, balance an account register, and calculate the cost of fees such as overdraft and ATM fees
lessons.key_concepts: Checking accounts for spending, savings accounts for earning interest; deposits, withdrawals, debit cards; account register running balance; pending transactions; overdraft fees and minimum-balance fees; deposit insurance at insured banks and credit unions up to a legal limit; online vs traditional banks
lessons.key_vocabulary: checking account, savings account, debit card, balance, overdraft, fee, register, credit union, deposit insurance
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes the 'available balance' in an app already reflects every check and pending charge; thinks a debit card works like a credit card and does not draw from their own money
lessons.real_world_hook: A $4 coffee that overdraws an account by $2 triggers an overdraft fee; calculate the effective cost of that coffee

lessons.learning_objective: Calculate simple interest and total amount using I = Prt and solve for any variable
lessons.key_concepts: I = Prt with P principal, r annual rate as a decimal, t time in years; total A = P + I = P(1 + rt); converting months to years; simple interest grows linearly; solving for r or t; uses in some short-term loans
lessons.key_vocabulary: principal, interest, interest rate, simple interest, term, linear growth
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses r = 5 instead of 0.05 for 5%; uses t = 18 for an 18-month loan instead of 1.5 years
lessons.real_world_hook: Borrowing $1,200 from a family member at 4% simple interest for 2 years

lessons.learning_objective: Calculate compound interest with A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), compare compounding frequencies, and connect compound growth to exponential functions
lessons.key_concepts: Interest earns interest; A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) with n compounding periods per year; continuous compounding A = Pe^(rt) as the limit; more frequent compounding gives slightly more, with diminishing gains; time matters more than frequency; compound vs simple growth over long periods
lessons.key_vocabulary: compound interest, compounding period, principal, exponential growth, continuous compounding
lessons.common_misconceptions: Computes monthly compounding as P(1 + r)^(12t) using the annual rate each month instead of r/12; thinks doubling the time doubles the interest earned under compounding
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing $2,000 left in a savings account for 10 years at the same rate compounded annually vs monthly

lessons.learning_objective: Compute and compare annual percentage yield (APY) across accounts and use the rule of 72 to estimate doubling time
lessons.key_concepts: APY = (1 + r/n)^n - 1 expresses the effective annual return including compounding, so it lets you compare accounts with different compounding; APY is at least the stated nominal rate; rule of 72: doubling time is approximately 72 divided by the percent rate, an estimate that works best for moderate rates; exact doubling time from logarithms t = ln 2 / ln(1 + r)
lessons.key_vocabulary: APY, nominal rate, effective rate, doubling time, rule of 72, estimate
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses the rule of 72 with the rate as a decimal (72 / 0.06 = 1,200 years); treats the rule of 72 as an exact answer instead of an approximation
lessons.real_world_hook: Two banks advertise savings accounts: one lists a rate compounded monthly, the other lists an APY; decide which earns more

lessons.lesson_title: Credit cards, APR, and minimum payments
lessons.learning_objective: Explain how credit card interest accrues, calculate monthly interest from APR, and analyze how paying only the minimum affects total cost and payoff time
lessons.key_concepts: APR is the annual rate; a monthly periodic rate is roughly APR/12; paying the full statement balance by the due date typically avoids interest on purchases (grace period); carrying a balance accrues interest each month; minimum payments are small relative to the balance, so much of the payment goes to interest and payoff can take years; late fees and penalty APRs; recursive model B_next = B(1 + APR/12) - payment
lessons.key_vocabulary: credit card, APR, periodic rate, balance, minimum payment, grace period, statement, late fee
lessons.common_misconceptions: Applies the full APR (for example 24%) to a monthly balance instead of about 2% per month; believes paying the minimum each month keeps a card interest-free
lessons.real_world_hook: A $1,500 laptop charged to a card: compare total paid if you pay it off in 3 months vs paying only the minimum

lessons.learning_objective: Describe what a credit report contains, the factors that shape a credit score, and how credit affects the cost of borrowing
lessons.key_concepts: A credit report lists accounts, balances, payment history, and inquiries; consumers can get free reports from the nationwide credit bureaus; credit scores (such as FICO and VantageScore) are calculated from report data, with payment history and amounts owed relative to limits (credit utilization) among the most important factors, plus length of history, new credit, and credit mix; a higher score generally means lower interest rates; checking your own score does not hurt it
lessons.key_vocabulary: credit report, credit score, credit bureau, payment history, credit utilization, hard inquiry, soft inquiry
lessons.common_misconceptions: Believes checking your own credit score lowers it; thinks carrying a balance and paying interest builds credit better than paying in full
lessons.real_world_hook: Calculating credit utilization for someone with a $900 balance on a $3,000 limit and seeing what paying it down to $300 does to the ratio

lessons.learning_objective: Use the loan payment formula and an amortization table to see how each payment splits between interest and principal and how term and rate affect total cost
lessons.key_concepts: Installment loans with fixed payments; monthly payment M = P(r/12)/(1 - (1 + r/12)^(-12t)); early payments are mostly interest, later ones mostly principal; total cost = payment x number of payments; longer term lowers the payment but raises total interest; extra principal payments shorten the loan; amortization schedules in a spreadsheet
lessons.key_vocabulary: loan, principal, installment, amortization, amortization schedule, term, total interest
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes each payment reduces the principal by the same amount; picks the loan with the lowest monthly payment as the cheapest without computing total paid
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a $15,000 loan over 3 years vs 6 years at the same rate: monthly payment vs total interest

lessons.lesson_title: Student loans and paying for college
lessons.learning_objective: Compare ways to pay for education, distinguish federal from private loans and subsidized from unsubsidized loans, and estimate repayment costs
lessons.ccss_code: Jump$tart: Credit & Debt / Financial Decision Making
lessons.key_concepts: Grants and scholarships do not need to be repaid; loans do; the FAFSA is the application for federal student aid; federal subsidized loans do not accrue interest while in school (for eligible students), unsubsidized loans do; private loans may require a cosigner and usually lack federal repayment options; interest capitalization; estimating payments with the loan formula; comparing expected debt to expected starting salary
lessons.key_vocabulary: FAFSA, grant, scholarship, subsidized loan, unsubsidized loan, private loan, cosigner, capitalization, repayment plan
lessons.common_misconceptions: Believes an unsubsidized loan costs nothing until graduation; treats a financial aid package's total, including loans, as free money
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing two college offers where one has a larger grant and the other a larger loan in the 'aid' total

lessons.learning_objective: Calculate the effect of inflation on purchasing power and distinguish nominal from real (inflation-adjusted) returns
lessons.key_concepts: Inflation is a general rise in prices, often measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI); future price = current price x (1 + i)^t; purchasing power falls when prices rise; real return is approximately nominal return minus inflation; money kept in cash loses purchasing power over time if inflation is positive
lessons.key_vocabulary: inflation, purchasing power, Consumer Price Index, nominal return, real return, deflation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Thinks a savings account earning 2% while prices rise 3% is growing in value; computes 10 years of 3% inflation as 30% instead of (1.03)^10 - 1, about 34%
lessons.real_world_hook: Estimating what a $5 meal might cost in 20 years at a steady 3% annual inflation rate

lessons.learning_objective: Model investment growth with exponential functions and future-value calculations to show the effect of starting early and contributing regularly
lessons.key_concepts: Exponential growth A = P(1 + r)^t for a lump sum; regular contributions grow as a geometric series (future value of an annuity); starting earlier gives more compounding periods; average annual return is not guaranteed and varies year to year, so use assumed rates as illustrations; using a spreadsheet or calculator to compare scenarios
lessons.prerequisites: Compound interest, exponential functions, geometric sequences
lessons.key_vocabulary: future value, lump sum, annuity, contribution, compounding, rate of return, time horizon
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes someone who invests for 10 years starting at 25 will always end up with less than someone who invests for 30 years starting at 35, because they contributed less in total; treats an illustrative assumed return as a guaranteed rate
lessons.real_world_hook: Two friends: one invests $100 a month from age 22 to 32 then stops, the other invests $100 a month from 32 to 62; compare at 62 under the same assumed return

lessons.lesson_title: Stocks, bonds, diversification, and index funds
lessons.learning_objective: Describe stocks, bonds, and funds, explain the risk-return trade-off and diversification, and compare the cost of fund fees over time
lessons.key_concepts: Stocks are ownership shares with higher expected return and higher volatility; bonds are loans to governments or companies with generally lower risk and return; mutual funds and ETFs pool many investments; index funds track a market index and often have low fees; diversification spreads risk across many holdings; expense ratios reduce returns every year and compound; past performance does not guarantee future results; expected value as a way to think about risk
lessons.key_vocabulary: stock, bond, mutual fund, ETF, index fund, diversification, risk, return, volatility, expense ratio
lessons.common_misconceptions: Believes owning several stocks in the same industry is diversified; thinks a 1% fee difference is trivial without computing its compounded effect over 30 years
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing $10,000 in a fund with a 0.05% expense ratio vs one with 1% over 30 years at the same gross return

lessons.learning_objective: Compare common retirement accounts and calculate the value of an employer match and tax-advantaged growth
lessons.key_concepts: Employer plans like 401(k) or 403(b) and individual accounts like IRAs; traditional (pre-tax contributions, taxed at withdrawal) vs Roth (after-tax contributions, qualified withdrawals tax-free); employer match as a percent of salary up to a limit; vesting; annual contribution limits set by law that change over time; early-withdrawal penalties
lessons.key_vocabulary: 401(k), IRA, Roth, traditional, employer match, vesting, contribution limit, tax-advantaged
lessons.common_misconceptions: Skips contributing enough to get the full employer match to 'have more take-home pay,' giving up an immediate 50-100% return on those dollars; thinks a Roth contribution reduces this year's taxes
lessons.real_world_hook: An employer matches 50% of contributions up to 6% of a $50,000 salary; how much free money is left on the table by contributing only 2%?

lessons.learning_objective: Calculate the total cost of owning a car, compare buying new vs used and loan terms, and account for depreciation and operating costs
lessons.key_concepts: Purchase price plus taxes and fees; down payment; auto loan payment and total interest by term; depreciation as exponential decay; operating costs (fuel, insurance, maintenance, registration); cost per mile; new vs used trade-offs; dealer focus on monthly payment can hide a longer term
lessons.key_vocabulary: down payment, auto loan, depreciation, total cost of ownership, cost per mile, term, trade-in
lessons.common_misconceptions: Compares two cars only by sticker price, ignoring fuel and insurance; agrees to a lower monthly payment that comes from stretching the loan from 48 to 72 months and thinks the car got cheaper
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a $28,000 new car with a $16,000 three-year-old version over five years of ownership

lessons.learning_objective: Compare the costs of renting and buying, including mortgage payments, down payments, and ongoing ownership costs
lessons.key_concepts: Renting: rent, security deposit, renter's insurance, flexibility; buying: down payment, closing costs, mortgage principal and interest, property tax, homeowner's insurance, maintenance, possible HOA fees; a common affordability guideline relates housing cost to gross income; equity builds as principal is paid; 15- vs 30-year mortgage total interest; break-even thinking over how long you stay
lessons.key_vocabulary: rent, security deposit, mortgage, down payment, closing costs, property tax, equity, homeowner's insurance, HOA
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes the monthly mortgage payment is the whole cost of owning a home, leaving out taxes, insurance, and maintenance; believes rent is always 'throwing money away' while all of a mortgage payment builds equity
lessons.real_world_hook: Deciding whether to rent a $1,600 apartment or buy a $300,000 condo for a job that may last only three years

lessons.learning_objective: Explain how insurance shares risk and compare plans using premiums, deductibles, copays, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket maximums
lessons.key_concepts: Insurance pools risk: many pay premiums so a few with losses are covered; premium is the regular cost; deductible is what you pay before coverage starts; copay and coinsurance after the deductible; out-of-pocket maximum caps costs in a year; higher deductible usually means a lower premium; types: health, auto (liability required in most states), renters, homeowners, life, disability; expected-value comparison of plans
lessons.key_vocabulary: insurance, premium, deductible, copay, coinsurance, out-of-pocket maximum, liability, claim, policy
lessons.common_misconceptions: Thinks the plan with the lowest premium is always cheapest; believes insurance pays the whole bill as soon as you file a claim, forgetting the deductible
lessons.real_world_hook: A $3,000 car repair after an accident with a $500 vs $1,000 deductible plan; which plan costs less over a year with and without the accident?

lessons.lesson_title: Capstone: making a major financial decision
lessons.learning_objective: Build a mathematical model comparing two financial choices, account for interest, inflation, and risk, and justify a recommendation
lessons.ccss_code: Jump$tart: Financial Decision Making / Mathematical Practice 4
lessons.key_concepts: Define the decision and the options; list all costs and benefits, including opportunity cost; model each option over time with linear, exponential, or loan formulas in a spreadsheet; sensitivity analysis by changing one assumption (rate, time, price); weigh non-numeric factors; present a recommendation with evidence
lessons.key_vocabulary: opportunity cost, model, assumption, sensitivity analysis, trade-off, recommendation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Ignores opportunity cost, treating money spent now as if it could not have grown elsewhere; presents one assumed interest rate as certain instead of testing a range
lessons.real_world_hook: Deciding whether to finance a car, lease it, or keep an old car and invest the difference for four years

lessons.learning_objective: Solve linear equations in one variable, including those with fractions and literal coefficients, and determine when an equation has no solution or infinitely many solutions
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Algebra: Linear equations in one variable
lessons.key_concepts: Distribute and combine like terms on each side, then isolate the variable; clear fractions by multiplying by the LCD; ax + b = cx + d has no solution when a = c and b is not d, infinitely many when a = c and b = d; solving for an expression like 3x - 2 directly instead of x; writing equations from word problems
lessons.prerequisites: Order of operations, distributive property, integer and fraction operations
lessons.key_vocabulary: linear equation, solution, no solution, infinitely many solutions, coefficient, constant term, literal equation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Distributes a negative to only the first term (-2(x - 3) = -2x - 3); solves for x when the question asks for the value of 2x + 1; concludes an equation like 3x + 5 = 3x + 5 has 'no solution' because x cancels
lessons.real_world_hook: SAT-style question: for what value of k does 4(x - k) = 4x + 12 have infinitely many solutions?

lessons.learning_objective: Write, interpret, and graph linear equations in two variables in slope-intercept, point-slope, and standard form, and interpret slope and intercepts in context
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Algebra: Linear equations in two variables
lessons.key_concepts: y = mx + b, y - y1 = m(x - x1), Ax + By = C; slope as rate of change in context; x- and y-intercepts; solutions are ordered pairs on the line; combinations problems like 5x + 8y = 200 (cost of two items)
lessons.prerequisites: Slope, graphing on the coordinate plane, solving one-variable equations
lessons.key_vocabulary: slope, y-intercept, x-intercept, slope-intercept form, standard form, ordered pair, rate of change
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads the slope of 3x + 2y = 12 as 3 instead of -3/2; interprets the y-intercept as the rate instead of the starting value; computes slope as run over rise
lessons.real_world_hook: A phone plan costing $25 per month plus $0.10 per text, written and interpreted as a line

lessons.learning_objective: Use function notation to evaluate, build, and interpret linear functions from tables, graphs, and context, including parallel and perpendicular lines
lessons.key_concepts: f(x) = mx + b; f(a) means output at input a; finding m from two points; constant rate of change in tables; parallel lines share slope, perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals; translating 'increases by 4 every 3 units' into slope 4/3
lessons.prerequisites: Linear equations in two variables, function notation basics
lessons.key_vocabulary: linear function, function notation, input, output, rate of change, parallel, perpendicular, negative reciprocal
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads f(3) as f times 3; uses the reciprocal without changing sign for a perpendicular slope; confuses f(x) = 5 (find x) with f(5) (find the output)
lessons.real_world_hook: Modeling a candle that burns down 0.4 inches per hour from a starting height of 9 inches

lessons.lesson_title: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
lessons.learning_objective: Solve systems of two linear equations by substitution, elimination, and graphing, determine the number of solutions, and model contexts with systems
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Algebra: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
lessons.key_concepts: Solution is the intersection point; elimination by scaling equations; substitution; one solution (different slopes), no solution (same slope, different intercepts), infinitely many (same line); finding a constant so a system has no solution; using Desmos to find the intersection
lessons.prerequisites: Linear equations in two variables, solving one-variable equations
lessons.key_vocabulary: system of equations, substitution, elimination, intersection, consistent, inconsistent, dependent
lessons.common_misconceptions: Stops after finding x when the question asks for x + y or for y; thinks parallel lines intersect at the origin; when setting a system to have no solution, sets the constants equal instead of the slopes
lessons.real_world_hook: Figuring out how many adult and student tickets were sold from total tickets and total revenue

lessons.lesson_title: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
lessons.learning_objective: Solve and graph linear inequalities and systems of linear inequalities, and interpret solutions in context including maximum and minimum values
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Algebra: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
lessons.key_concepts: Solve like an equation but flip the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative; shaded half-planes; solid vs dashed boundary lines; testing whether a point satisfies a system; translating 'at least' and 'no more than'; integer constraints in context
lessons.key_vocabulary: inequality, half-plane, boundary line, at least, at most, no more than, solution region
lessons.common_misconceptions: Forgets to flip the sign when dividing by a negative; translates 'at least 20' as x < 20; rounds a context answer the wrong way (needs 7.2 buses and answers 7)
lessons.real_world_hook: Budgeting: buying shirts at $12 and hats at $8 without spending more than $100

lessons.learning_objective: Rewrite polynomial expressions by expanding, combining like terms, and factoring, including difference of squares and perfect square trinomials, to identify equivalent forms
lessons.key_concepts: Multiplying binomials and polynomials; factoring GCF, trinomials, difference of squares a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b), perfect squares (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2; matching coefficients to find unknown constants; recognizing structure (x^4 - 16 as a difference of squares)
lessons.prerequisites: Distributive property, combining like terms, integer operations
lessons.key_vocabulary: polynomial, binomial, trinomial, factor, expand, difference of squares, perfect square trinomial, equivalent form
lessons.common_misconceptions: Writes (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2; drops the middle term or the sign when expanding (x - 3)^2 = x^2 - 9; when matching coefficients, matches terms of different degrees
lessons.real_world_hook: SAT-style question: if (ax - 2)(2x + b) = 6x^2 + 5x - 6 for all x, find a + b

lessons.lesson_title: Equivalent Expressions: Exponents, Radicals, and Rational Expressions
lessons.learning_objective: Rewrite expressions using exponent rules, rational exponents, and radicals, and simplify and combine rational expressions
lessons.key_concepts: x^a * x^b = x^(a+b), (x^a)^b = x^(ab), x^(-n) = 1/x^n, x^(m/n) = nth root of x^m; simplifying rational expressions by factoring and canceling common factors; adding rational expressions with a common denominator; rewriting to reveal a quantity
lessons.key_vocabulary: exponent, rational exponent, radical, rational expression, common factor, simplify
lessons.common_misconceptions: Writes x^2 * x^3 = x^6 or (x^3)^2 = x^5; cancels terms instead of factors ((x + 3)/3 = x); treats x^(-2) as a negative number
lessons.real_world_hook: Rewriting a compound-interest expression to read off the monthly growth rate

lessons.learning_objective: Interpret and use quadratic functions in standard, vertex, and factored forms to find the vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts, and maximum or minimum values
lessons.key_concepts: Standard form ax^2 + bx + c (y-intercept c, vertex x = -b/(2a)); vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k (vertex (h, k)); factored form a(x - p)(x - q) (x-intercepts p, q); sign of a gives opening direction; axis of symmetry halfway between zeros; projectile models
lessons.key_vocabulary: quadratic function, parabola, vertex, axis of symmetry, zeros, roots, x-intercepts, maximum, minimum
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads the vertex of y = (x - 3)^2 + 2 as (-3, 2); confuses the x-intercepts with the vertex; thinks the y-intercept of factored form a(x - p)(x - q) is a
lessons.real_world_hook: Finding the maximum height of a ball thrown upward modeled by h(t) = -16t^2 + 48t + 5

lessons.lesson_title: Nonlinear Functions: Exponential Models and Transformations
lessons.learning_objective: Build and interpret exponential growth and decay functions, distinguish linear from exponential change, and interpret function transformations and graphs
lessons.key_concepts: f(t) = a(1 + r)^t and a(1 - r)^t; growth factor vs growth rate; a(b)^(t/k) for change every k units; linear change adds a constant, exponential change multiplies; transformations f(x) + k, f(x - h), -f(x); reading features from graphs and tables
lessons.prerequisites: Percent increase and decrease, exponent rules, function notation
lessons.key_vocabulary: exponential growth, exponential decay, growth factor, growth rate, initial value, half-life, transformation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads 0.85 in 1200(0.85)^t as an 85% decrease instead of 15%; thinks f(x - 2) shifts the graph left 2; models a constant percent change with a linear function
lessons.real_world_hook: A car losing 15% of its value every year

lessons.lesson_title: Nonlinear Equations in One Variable and Systems in Two Variables
lessons.learning_objective: Solve quadratic, radical, rational, and absolute value equations, use the discriminant to count solutions, and solve systems of a linear and a nonlinear equation
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Advanced Math: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
lessons.key_concepts: Solve quadratics by factoring, square roots, completing the square, or the quadratic formula; discriminant b^2 - 4ac (positive: 2 real solutions, zero: 1, negative: 0); check for extraneous solutions with radicals and rationals; substitute a linear equation into a quadratic; sum of roots -b/a and product c/a; using Desmos to find intersections
lessons.key_vocabulary: quadratic formula, discriminant, extraneous solution, linear-quadratic system, completing the square, real solutions
lessons.common_misconceptions: Misapplies the zero-product property to nonzero products ((x - 2)(x - 3) = 6 so x = 8 or 9); divides both sides by x and loses the solution x = 0; uses -b^2 instead of b^2 in the discriminant when b is negative
lessons.real_world_hook: SAT-style question: for what value of c does the line y = 4 intersect y = x^2 - 6x + c at exactly one point?

lessons.lesson_title: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
lessons.learning_objective: Solve multistep problems with ratios, rates, proportions, and unit conversions, including derived units like density and speed
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
lessons.key_concepts: Set up proportions with matching units; unit rates; dimensional analysis by multiplying conversion factors so units cancel; converting squared and cubed units (1 ft^2 = 144 in^2); density = mass/volume; scale
lessons.prerequisites: Ratios and unit rates, fraction operations
lessons.key_vocabulary: ratio, rate, proportion, unit conversion, conversion factor, dimensional analysis, density
lessons.common_misconceptions: Converts square feet to square inches by multiplying by 12 instead of 144; flips the conversion factor so units do not cancel; adds to both parts of a ratio instead of scaling
lessons.real_world_hook: Converting a recipe for 4 into one for 10 and changing cups to milliliters

lessons.learning_objective: Solve percent problems including percent of a quantity, percent increase and decrease, reverse percent, and successive percent changes
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis: Percentages
lessons.key_concepts: Part = percent x whole; percent change = (new - old)/old; multipliers 1 + r and 1 - r; successive changes multiply; finding the original from a final value by dividing by the multiplier; p% of q equals q% of p
lessons.key_vocabulary: percent, percent increase, percent decrease, multiplier, original value, percentage point
lessons.common_misconceptions: Divides by the new value instead of the original for percent change; adds successive percents (up 20% then down 20% means no change); finds an original price by subtracting the percent from the final price
lessons.real_world_hook: A jacket is $68 after a 15% discount: what was the original price?

lessons.lesson_title: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
lessons.learning_objective: Calculate and compare mean, median, range, and standard deviation conceptually, and interpret dot plots, histograms, and box plots
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
lessons.key_concepts: Mean is pulled by outliers more than the median; effect of adding or removing a value on mean and median; standard deviation measures spread (compare qualitatively, no computation needed); reading frequency tables and histograms; using total = mean x count
lessons.key_vocabulary: mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation, outlier, distribution, skewed, frequency table
lessons.common_misconceptions: Finds the median of a frequency table by taking the middle of the listed values instead of the middle data point; thinks removing an outlier changes the median more than the mean; assumes a larger range always means a larger standard deviation
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing two classes' test scores when one class has a single very low score

lessons.learning_objective: Interpret scatterplots, lines and curves of best fit, and linear vs exponential models, and compute probabilities and conditional probabilities from two-way tables
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis: Two-variable data: models and scatterplots; Probability and conditional probability
lessons.key_concepts: Slope and y-intercept of a line of best fit in context; predicting from a model and residual meaning (actual minus predicted); choosing linear vs exponential fit; probability = favorable/total; conditional probability P(A given B) uses only the row or column for B as the denominator
lessons.key_vocabulary: scatterplot, line of best fit, residual, association, two-way table, probability, conditional probability
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses the grand total instead of the conditional row or column total for P(A given B); confuses P(A given B) with P(B given A); claims a correlation proves causation
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a two-way table of students by grade and favorite lunch option

lessons.lesson_title: Inference, Margin of Error, and Evaluating Statistical Claims
lessons.learning_objective: Use sample statistics and margins of error to make inferences about populations, and evaluate claims based on study design, random sampling, and random assignment
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error; Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
lessons.key_concepts: A sample estimate plus or minus the margin of error gives a plausible interval for the population value; larger random samples give smaller margins of error; random sampling allows generalizing to the population sampled; random assignment allows cause-and-effect conclusions; observational studies show only association
lessons.key_vocabulary: sample, population, margin of error, random sample, random assignment, observational study, experiment, bias
lessons.common_misconceptions: Says a 52% result with a 3% margin of error proves a majority; generalizes results from volunteers or one school to all teenagers; claims causation from an observational study
lessons.real_world_hook: Deciding whether a poll of 400 likely voters supports a headline claim

lessons.learning_objective: Compute area, surface area, and volume of two- and three-dimensional figures, including composite figures and the effect of scaling dimensions
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Geometry and Trigonometry: Area and volume
lessons.key_concepts: Area of rectangles, triangles, circles, trapezoids; volume of prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres, pyramids (formulas on the SAT reference sheet); surface area; scaling lengths by k scales area by k^2 and volume by k^3; working backward from a volume to a dimension
lessons.key_vocabulary: area, perimeter, surface area, volume, cylinder, cone, sphere, scale factor
lessons.common_misconceptions: Thinks doubling all dimensions doubles the volume (it multiplies by 8); uses diameter in place of radius in pi r^2; confuses surface area with volume
lessons.real_world_hook: How much water a cylindrical tank holds if its radius is doubled

lessons.learning_objective: Apply angle relationships from parallel lines and transversals, triangle angle sums, congruence, and similar triangles to find unknown measures
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Geometry and Trigonometry: Lines, angles, and triangles
lessons.key_concepts: Vertical angles equal; linear pairs sum to 180; alternate interior and corresponding angles equal for parallel lines; triangle angles sum to 180; exterior angle equals sum of remote interiors; similar triangles have proportional sides; isosceles triangle base angles; triangle inequality
lessons.key_vocabulary: vertical angles, supplementary, transversal, alternate interior angles, corresponding angles, similar triangles, congruent
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes a figure is drawn to scale and measures it by eye; matches non-corresponding sides when setting up a similar-triangle proportion; assumes lines are parallel without being told
lessons.real_world_hook: Using shadows and similar triangles to find the height of a flagpole

lessons.learning_objective: Solve right triangles using the Pythagorean theorem, special right triangles, and sine, cosine, and tangent, and use the relationship sin x = cos(90 - x)
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Geometry and Trigonometry: Right triangles and trigonometry
lessons.key_concepts: a^2 + b^2 = c^2; Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13); 30-60-90 sides x, x*sqrt(3), 2x and 45-45-90 sides x, x, x*sqrt(2); SOH-CAH-TOA; complementary angle identity sin x = cos(90 - x); radian and degree conversion; similar triangles share trig ratios
lessons.key_vocabulary: Pythagorean theorem, hypotenuse, sine, cosine, tangent, special right triangle, complementary angles, radian
lessons.common_misconceptions: Applies the Pythagorean theorem to non-right triangles or uses the hypotenuse as a leg; mixes up opposite and adjacent relative to the given angle; puts sqrt(3) on the wrong leg of a 30-60-90 triangle
lessons.real_world_hook: Finding the length of a wheelchair ramp that rises 2 feet at a 5-degree angle

lessons.learning_objective: Use circle equations, arc length, sector area, central and inscribed angles, and radians, including completing the square to find center and radius
lessons.key_concepts: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2; completing the square on x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0; arc length = (central angle/360) x 2 pi r or r * theta in radians; sector area proportion; inscribed angle is half the central angle; tangent is perpendicular to the radius
lessons.prerequisites: Completing the square, area and circumference, proportions
lessons.key_vocabulary: center, radius, circle equation, arc length, sector, central angle, inscribed angle, radian, tangent line
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads r^2 as the radius (radius 25 from (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 25); takes the center of (x + 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 16 as (3, -2); forgets to add the completed-square constants to both sides
lessons.real_world_hook: SAT-style question: find the radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y = 0

lessons.lesson_title: Digital SAT Format and Module Adaptivity
lessons.learning_objective: Explain the structure of the digital SAT Math section and how multistage adaptive testing affects strategy
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Strategy: Test format and multistage adaptive testing
lessons.key_concepts: Math section has two modules of 22 questions with 35 minutes each (44 questions, 70 minutes); module 1 has a mix of difficulties and performance there routes the student to an easier or harder module 2; the harder module 2 is required for top scores; each module contains unscored pretest questions that look like the others; no penalty for wrong answers; scores range 200 to 800; questions are in four domains (Algebra and Advanced Math about 35% each, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis and Geometry and Trigonometry about 15% each)
lessons.prerequisites: Familiarity with the four SAT math domains
lessons.key_vocabulary: module, adaptive testing, routing, pretest question, scaled score, Bluebook
lessons.common_misconceptions: Thinks module 1 does not matter much, so rushes it; tries to identify and skip pretest questions; believes a harder-feeling module 2 means they are doing badly
lessons.real_world_hook: Taking a full practice test in the College Board Bluebook app

lessons.learning_objective: Use the built-in Desmos graphing calculator to solve equations, systems, and quadratic problems faster and to check algebraic work
lessons.key_concepts: Desmos is available for the entire Math section; graph both sides of an equation and find intersections; click to find zeros, vertex, and intersection points; use sliders for unknown constants; regression with tables (y1 ~ mx1 + b) for data questions; type expressions to compare equivalent forms; know when mental algebra is faster
lessons.prerequisites: Linear and quadratic functions, systems of equations
lessons.key_vocabulary: graphing calculator, intersection, zero, vertex, slider, regression, window
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses Desmos for every question even when mental math is faster; misreads a rounded decimal from the graph instead of using an exact fraction; forgets to zoom out and misses a second intersection
lessons.real_world_hook: Solving a system in 20 seconds by graphing both lines

lessons.learning_objective: Enter answers to student-produced response questions correctly, including fractions, decimals, and negative values
lessons.key_concepts: About a quarter of math questions are student-produced responses with no choices; up to 5 characters for a positive answer and 6 for a negative answer (including the sign); fractions like 7/2 or decimals are accepted, mixed numbers are not; long decimals should fill all available spaces (truncate or round); if multiple answers are correct, enter only one
lessons.key_vocabulary: student-produced response, grid-in, mixed number, improper fraction, truncate, round
lessons.common_misconceptions: Enters 3 1/2 as a mixed number, which is read as 31/2; rounds 2/3 to 0.6 or 0.67 instead of filling the spaces as .6666 or .6667; leaves the answer blank instead of guessing
lessons.real_world_hook: Entering a fractional answer like 11/4 exactly

lessons.lesson_title: Pacing, Triage, and the Reference Sheet
lessons.learning_objective: Plan pacing for 35-minute modules, triage questions using flag-and-return, and use the reference sheet and answer-elimination strategies
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Strategy: Pacing and question triage
lessons.key_concepts: About 1.5 minutes per question on average; skip and flag time-consuming questions then return; never leave a question blank since there is no guessing penalty; the reference sheet lists area, volume, special right triangles, and the number of degrees and radians in a circle; backsolving from answer choices; plugging in numbers for variable choices; reading the final question to answer what is asked
lessons.key_vocabulary: pacing, triage, flag for review, backsolving, plugging in numbers, reference sheet, process of elimination
lessons.common_misconceptions: Spends 5 minutes on one hard question early and runs out of time; ignores the reference sheet and misremembers formulas; answers for x when the question asks for 2x or x + 3
lessons.real_world_hook: Building a personal timing plan for test day

lessons.learning_objective: Analyze practice test results by SAT skill, classify errors as content, careless, or timing, and build a targeted study plan
lessons.ccss_code: SAT Strategy: Score report and error analysis
lessons.key_concepts: Score reports break performance down by domain and skill; keep an error log listing the skill, the error type, and the corrected reasoning; redo missed questions without looking; prioritize high-frequency domains (Algebra and Advanced Math) and the most-missed skills; retest under timed conditions
lessons.prerequisites: Completion of at least one practice module
lessons.key_vocabulary: error log, content error, careless error, timing error, skill, domain, score report
lessons.common_misconceptions: Only checks the right answer without understanding why their choice was wrong; studies only favorite topics; takes practice tests without reviewing them
lessons.real_world_hook: Turning a practice test into a two-week study plan

lessons.lesson_title: How the ACT Math test works
lessons.learning_objective: Describe the format, timing, scoring, and content blueprint of the enhanced ACT Math section and set a personal score goal
lessons.key_concepts: Enhanced ACT Math section: 45 questions in 50 minutes (about 67 seconds per question); 41 questions are scored and the rest are embedded field-test items you cannot identify, so treat every question as if it counts; every question is multiple choice with four answer choices (reduced from five on the legacy test); a permitted calculator may be used on the entire math section (check ACT's calculator policy for banned models such as computer-algebra calculators); the section score is on a 1-36 scale and the Composite averages English, math, and reading (science is optional and is not in the Composite); reporting categories: Preparing for Higher Mathematics about 80% (Number & Quantity 10-12%, Algebra 17-20%, Functions 17-20%, Geometry 17-20%, Statistics & Probability 12-15%), Integrating Essential Skills about 20% (rates, percents, proportional reasoning, area and volume, averages and medians), plus a Modeling label applied to questions that also count in other categories; content covers math typically learned up to the start of grade 12
lessons.prerequisites: Algebra 1, Geometry, and most of Algebra 2
lessons.key_vocabulary: section score, Composite score, reporting category, Preparing for Higher Mathematics, Integrating Essential Skills, Modeling, field-test item, permitted calculator
lessons.common_misconceptions: Assumes the enhanced ACT still has five answer choices and 60 questions in 60 minutes (the legacy format); believes science counts toward the Composite on the enhanced test; skips questions because they think an unanswered question is safer than a wrong one
lessons.real_world_hook: A junior who took the legacy ACT practice book plans their pacing for 60 questions in 60 minutes and has to recalculate for 45 questions in 50 minutes

lessons.learning_objective: Use a two-pass pacing plan, answer-choice elimination, backsolving, and picking numbers to maximize correct answers in 50 minutes
lessons.key_concepts: Scores count correct answers only, so never leave a bubble blank (a blind guess on four choices has a 25% chance); two-pass approach: answer quick questions first, flag time-sinks, return with remaining time; do not assume question order matches difficulty, so skip anything slow and come back; backsolving: plug answer choices into the problem starting with a middle value; picking numbers for variable-in-the-answer questions; estimating and eliminating impossible choices (negative lengths, probabilities over 1); using the calculator to check, not to replace, algebra; checking what the question actually asks (x vs 2x + 1, perimeter vs area)
lessons.prerequisites: How the ACT Math test works
lessons.key_vocabulary: pacing, two-pass strategy, backsolving, picking numbers, elimination, estimation, letter-of-the-day guess
lessons.common_misconceptions: Spends four minutes fighting one hard geometry question and leaves the last eight questions blank instead of guessing on them; when backsolving, plugs in every choice from the first one instead of starting in the middle and using whether the result is too big or too small
lessons.real_world_hook: With 6 minutes left and 9 questions unanswered, a student decides which 4 to attempt and fills a guess for the other 5 before time is called

lessons.lesson_title: Percents, percent change, and successive percents
lessons.learning_objective: Solve percent, percent increase and decrease, and successive percent change problems, including finding the original amount
lessons.key_concepts: Percent of a number (part = percent x whole); percent change = (new - old)/old; multipliers: increase by r% means multiply by (1 + r), decrease means (1 - r); successive changes multiply, they do not add; reverse percent: original = final / multiplier; percent of a percent
lessons.key_vocabulary: percent, percent increase, percent decrease, multiplier, original amount, successive discount, markup
lessons.common_misconceptions: Thinks a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease returns to the original price (it is 0.96 of the original); finds the original price of a $60 item that was 25% off by adding 25% of 60 to get $75 instead of dividing 60 by 0.75 to get $80
lessons.real_world_hook: A jacket is marked down 30%, then an extra 10% comes off at the register; is that really 40% off?

lessons.lesson_title: Ratios, rates, proportions, and unit conversion
lessons.learning_objective: Set up and solve proportions and multi-step rate problems, including unit conversions and scale drawings
lessons.key_concepts: Part-to-part vs part-to-whole ratios; scaling a ratio (3:5 means 3k and 5k, total 8k); unit rates; dimensional analysis by multiplying by conversion factors equal to 1; distance = rate x time; work problems; scale drawings and map scales; squaring or cubing the scale factor for area or volume units (1 ft^2 = 144 in^2)
lessons.prerequisites: Fractions, multiplication and division of decimals
lessons.key_vocabulary: ratio, rate, unit rate, proportion, conversion factor, dimensional analysis, scale factor
lessons.common_misconceptions: Given boys to girls is 3:5 in a class of 32, divides 32 by 3 instead of by 8 (total parts); converts 2 square yards to square feet by multiplying by 3 instead of 9
lessons.real_world_hook: Converting a recipe that serves 4 into one that serves 10, then converting cups to tablespoons

lessons.learning_objective: Compute and reason about mean, median, mode, and weighted averages, including finding a missing value needed for a target average
lessons.key_concepts: Sum = mean x count, the key move for missing-value problems; weighted average = sum(weight x value)/sum(weights); median requires ordering and averaging the two middle values for an even count; effect of adding or removing a value; effect of outliers on mean vs median
lessons.key_vocabulary: mean, median, mode, range, weighted average, outlier, sum
lessons.common_misconceptions: To find the score needed on a fifth test for an 85 average after scores of 80, 82, 88, 90, averages the four scores and the target instead of using 5 x 85 = 425 minus the current sum 340 to get 85; finds the median of an unordered list by taking the middle entry as written
lessons.real_world_hook: A class grade where tests are worth 60% and homework 40%: what test average is needed for a B?

lessons.lesson_title: Area, surface area, and volume essentials
lessons.learning_objective: Find area and perimeter of composite figures and surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, cones, and spheres
lessons.ccss_code: ACT IES: Area, surface area, and volume / 7.G.B.6, G-GMD.A.3
lessons.key_concepts: Area formulas for rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapezoids, circles; composite figures by adding and subtracting pieces; surface area as the sum of face areas; volume of prism and cylinder = base area x height; cone = 1/3 base area x height; sphere = 4/3 pi r^3; scaling all dimensions by k multiplies area by k^2 and volume by k^3; plan to know common formulas from memory
lessons.key_vocabulary: area, perimeter, surface area, volume, base, composite figure, lateral area, scale factor
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses the diameter instead of the radius in pi r^2; says doubling every edge of a box doubles its volume (it multiplies volume by 8); uses the slant height instead of the perpendicular height in a cone's volume
lessons.real_world_hook: How many cubic feet of soil fill a cylindrical planter 3 ft across and 2 ft deep?

lessons.lesson_title: Linear equations, inequalities, and absolute value
lessons.learning_objective: Solve multi-step linear equations, linear inequalities, and absolute value equations and inequalities, and translate word problems into equations
lessons.key_concepts: Distribute and combine like terms; clear fractions with the LCD; flip the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative; |x - a| = b splits into x - a = b or x - a = -b; |x - a| < b means -b < x - a < b (between), |x - a| > b means outside; no solution and infinitely many solutions cases; solving literal equations for a variable
lessons.key_vocabulary: linear equation, inequality, absolute value, compound inequality, literal equation, solution set
lessons.common_misconceptions: Forgets to reverse the inequality sign in -3x > 12, writing x > -4; solves |2x - 1| = 7 and reports only x = 4, missing x = -3
lessons.real_world_hook: A taxi charges $3.50 plus $2.25 per mile; how far can you ride on $25?

lessons.lesson_title: Linear functions, slope, and coordinate geometry
lessons.learning_objective: Write and interpret linear functions in slope-intercept, point-slope, and standard form and use slope, distance, and midpoint in the coordinate plane
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Algebra / F-LE.A.2, G-GPE.B.5, G-GPE.B.7
lessons.key_concepts: Slope = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1); y = mx + b, y - y1 = m(x - x1), Ax + By = C with slope -A/B; parallel lines have equal slopes, perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals; slope and intercept in context; midpoint ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2); distance formula from the Pythagorean theorem
lessons.key_vocabulary: slope, y-intercept, x-intercept, point-slope form, standard form, parallel, perpendicular, midpoint, distance formula
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads the slope of 2x + 3y = 6 as 2; writes the perpendicular slope to 2/3 as 3/2 instead of -3/2; subtracts coordinates in opposite orders in the numerator and denominator of the slope formula
lessons.real_world_hook: A gym charges a $50 joining fee plus $30 a month; interpret the slope and y-intercept of the cost line

lessons.learning_objective: Solve systems of two linear equations by substitution, elimination, and graphing, and determine when a system has no solution or infinitely many
lessons.key_concepts: Substitution and elimination; graphical meaning of a solution as the intersection point; parallel lines give no solution, identical lines give infinitely many; finding k so a system has no solution (equal slopes, different intercepts); setting up systems from mixture, ticket, and coin problems
lessons.key_vocabulary: system of equations, substitution, elimination, intersection, consistent, inconsistent, dependent
lessons.common_misconceptions: After eliminating to get 0 = 5, concludes the solution is x = 0; when multiplying an equation by -2 for elimination, multiplies only the x-term and not the constant
lessons.real_world_hook: A theater sells adult tickets for $12 and student tickets for $8; 300 tickets bring in $3,000; how many of each sold?

lessons.learning_objective: Solve quadratic equations by factoring, square roots, completing the square, and the quadratic formula, and connect roots, vertex, and graph
lessons.key_concepts: Standard form ax^2 + bx + c, vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k, factored form a(x - r)(x - s); zero product property; quadratic formula and discriminant b^2 - 4ac (two, one, or no real roots); vertex x = -b/(2a); sum of roots -b/a and product c/a; difference of squares and perfect square trinomials; maximum or minimum in projectile and area problems
lessons.key_vocabulary: quadratic, root, zero, x-intercept, vertex, axis of symmetry, discriminant, factored form, vertex form
lessons.common_misconceptions: Solves x^2 = 5x by dividing both sides by x and loses the root x = 0; reads the vertex of y = (x + 3)^2 - 2 as (3, -2) instead of (-3, -2); applies the zero product property to (x - 2)(x + 1) = 6 by setting each factor equal to 6
lessons.real_world_hook: A ball's height is h(t) = -16t^2 + 48t + 4; when does it reach its maximum height and what is it?

lessons.lesson_title: Exponents, radicals, polynomials, and rational expressions
lessons.learning_objective: Simplify expressions using exponent rules, rational exponents, and radicals, and add, multiply, divide, and factor polynomial and rational expressions
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Number & Quantity and Algebra / N-RN.A.2, A-APR.A.1, A-APR.D.6
lessons.key_concepts: Product, quotient, and power rules; x^0 = 1; negative exponents mean reciprocals; x^(m/n) = nth root of x^m; simplifying radicals and rationalizing denominators; multiplying binomials and special products; factoring GCF, trinomials, difference of squares, grouping; simplifying rational expressions by canceling common factors (not terms); excluded values
lessons.prerequisites: Order of operations, integer exponents, factoring basics
lessons.key_vocabulary: exponent, base, rational exponent, radical, polynomial, binomial, rational expression, excluded value
lessons.common_misconceptions: Writes (x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 9; cancels the x terms in (x + 5)/x to get 5; evaluates 8^(2/3) as 16/3 instead of 4
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing 2^10 and 10^3 to see why computer memory sizes like 1,024 bytes sit near 1,000

lessons.lesson_title: Function notation, domain, range, and composition
lessons.learning_objective: Evaluate, interpret, and compose functions, find domain and range, and read function values from graphs and tables
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Functions / F-IF.A.1, F-IF.A.2, F-BF.A.1.C
lessons.key_concepts: f(a) is the output at input a; reading f(2) and solving f(x) = 2 from a graph; f(g(x)) means apply g first, then f; domain restrictions from division by zero and even roots; range from graphs; inverse functions swap inputs and outputs; vertical line test
lessons.key_vocabulary: function, input, output, domain, range, composition, inverse function, vertical line test
lessons.common_misconceptions: Computes f(g(2)) by applying f first; reads f(x) = 3 on a graph as the point where x = 3 instead of finding the x-values where the height is 3; treats f^-1(x) as 1/f(x)
lessons.real_world_hook: Converting a temperature with C(F) = (5/9)(F - 32) and then a sales-tax function on a price in another currency, as a composition

lessons.learning_objective: Describe how transformations change a graph and interpret piecewise functions and the zeros and end behavior of polynomial functions
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Functions / F-BF.B.3, F-IF.C.7.B, F-IF.C.7.C
lessons.key_concepts: f(x) + k shifts up, f(x - h) shifts right, -f(x) reflects over the x-axis, af(x) stretches vertically; piecewise functions choose a rule by input interval, with open and closed endpoints; absolute value graph y = a|x - h| + k; polynomial zeros and multiplicity (even multiplicity touches, odd crosses); end behavior from the leading term
lessons.prerequisites: Function notation, graphing linear and quadratic functions
lessons.key_vocabulary: transformation, translation, reflection, vertical stretch, piecewise function, zero, multiplicity, end behavior
lessons.common_misconceptions: Shifts f(x - 4) four units left instead of right; when evaluating a piecewise function at a boundary like x = 2, uses the piece with the open circle at 2
lessons.real_world_hook: A phone plan charges $40 for up to 5 GB and $10 for each additional GB, written as a piecewise function

lessons.learning_objective: Write, evaluate, and interpret exponential functions for growth and decay, including percent rate and half-life, and distinguish them from linear models
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Functions / F-LE.A.1, F-LE.A.2, F-LE.B.5
lessons.key_concepts: y = a(b)^x with a the initial value and b the growth factor; b = 1 + r for growth and 1 - r for decay; half-life and doubling-time forms like a(1/2)^(t/h); compound interest A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt); linear grows by equal differences, exponential by equal ratios; interpreting a and b in context
lessons.key_vocabulary: exponential function, initial value, growth factor, decay factor, growth rate, half-life, compound interest
lessons.common_misconceptions: Writes 5% decay as y = a(0.05)^x instead of a(0.95)^x; assumes a quantity that doubles every 3 years has the model a(2)^(3t) instead of a(2)^(t/3)
lessons.real_world_hook: A medication's amount in the body falls by 20% every hour after a 500 mg dose; how much remains after 4 hours?

lessons.learning_objective: Use angle relationships, triangle properties, congruence, and similarity to find missing angles and lengths
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Geometry / G-CO.C.9, G-CO.C.10, G-SRT.B.5
lessons.key_concepts: Vertical, supplementary, and complementary angles; parallel lines cut by a transversal (alternate interior, corresponding); triangle angle sum 180 degrees and exterior angle theorem; polygon interior angle sum (n - 2)180; isosceles and equilateral triangles; triangle inequality; similar triangles have proportional sides; congruence criteria SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS
lessons.key_vocabulary: vertical angles, transversal, alternate interior angles, exterior angle, similar, congruent, proportional, triangle inequality
lessons.common_misconceptions: Sets up a similarity proportion by matching sides in the order they are drawn instead of corresponding sides; uses 360 as the interior angle sum of every polygon
lessons.real_world_hook: Measuring a tree's height using its shadow and the shadow of a 6-foot person at the same time of day

lessons.lesson_title: Right triangles and special right triangles
lessons.learning_objective: Apply the Pythagorean theorem, Pythagorean triples, and 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 relationships to solve for missing lengths
lessons.key_concepts: a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with c the hypotenuse; common triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and their multiples; 45-45-90 sides x, x, x sqrt2; 30-60-90 sides x, x sqrt3, 2x with the short leg opposite 30 degrees; diagonals of squares and rectangles; altitude of an equilateral triangle; converse to test for a right triangle
lessons.key_vocabulary: hypotenuse, leg, Pythagorean theorem, Pythagorean triple, 45-45-90 triangle, 30-60-90 triangle
lessons.common_misconceptions: Adds the hypotenuse squared to a leg squared when finding a missing leg; in a 30-60-90 triangle puts the sqrt3 side opposite the 30 degree angle
lessons.real_world_hook: How long must a ladder be to reach a window 12 feet up if its base sits 5 feet from the wall?

lessons.lesson_title: Circles: arcs, sectors, and circle equations
lessons.learning_objective: Find arc length, sector area, and inscribed angle measures, and write and analyze the equation of a circle in the coordinate plane
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Geometry / G-C.A.2, G-C.B.5, G-GPE.A.1
lessons.key_concepts: Circumference 2 pi r and area pi r^2; arc length and sector area as a fraction (central angle/360) of the whole; inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc; tangent is perpendicular to the radius; (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2; completing the square to find center and radius from expanded form
lessons.prerequisites: Area and circumference, completing the square
lessons.key_vocabulary: radius, diameter, central angle, inscribed angle, arc length, sector, tangent, center-radius form
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads the radius of (x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 25 as 25 instead of 5, and the center as (2, 1) instead of (2, -1); sets an inscribed angle equal to its arc instead of half of it
lessons.real_world_hook: A pizza slice cut with a 45 degree central angle from a 16-inch pizza: how much crust and how much pizza?

lessons.lesson_title: Trigonometric ratios, the unit circle, and trig equations
lessons.learning_objective: Use sine, cosine, and tangent to solve right triangles, use the unit circle and radians for common angles, and apply the laws of sines and cosines when given
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Geometry / G-SRT.C.6, G-SRT.C.8, F-TF.A.2
lessons.key_concepts: SOH-CAH-TOA; sin and cos of complementary angles are equal; inverse trig to find angles; sin^2 + cos^2 = 1; tan = sin/cos; radians: 180 degrees = pi; unit circle values for 30, 45, 60, 90 degree families and signs by quadrant; amplitude and period of y = a sin(bx); law of sines and law of cosines for non-right triangles (often provided in the question); check calculator degree vs radian mode
lessons.key_vocabulary: sine, cosine, tangent, opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse, radian, unit circle, amplitude, period, law of sines, law of cosines
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses the adjacent side over the hypotenuse for sine; computes sin 30 with the calculator in radian mode and gets -0.988; given sin A = 3/5 in a right triangle, reports cos A = 5/3
lessons.real_world_hook: Finding the height of a kite flying on 100 feet of string at a 40 degree angle of elevation

lessons.learning_objective: Solve problems with volume, surface area, cross sections, and diagonals of three-dimensional figures, including composite solids
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Geometry / G-GMD.A.3, G-GMD.B.4, G-MG.A.1
lessons.key_concepts: Volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres; space diagonal of a box sqrt(l^2 + w^2 + h^2); cross sections of solids; rotating a 2D shape produces a solid; composite solids and hollow shapes; density = mass/volume; rates of filling a tank
lessons.prerequisites: Area, surface area, and volume essentials; Pythagorean theorem
lessons.key_vocabulary: prism, pyramid, cylinder, cone, sphere, cross section, space diagonal, density
lessons.common_misconceptions: Finds the space diagonal of a box by adding the three edge lengths; includes the area of the circle where two solids are glued together when finding the surface area of a composite solid
lessons.real_world_hook: Will a 40-inch fishing rod fit diagonally in a box that is 30 by 20 by 15 inches?

lessons.lesson_title: Complex numbers and the real number system
lessons.learning_objective: Classify numbers, perform operations with complex numbers, and recognize complex solutions to quadratic equations
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Number & Quantity / N-CN.A.1, N-CN.A.2, N-CN.C.7
lessons.key_concepts: Natural, integer, rational, irrational, real, complex; i = sqrt(-1) and i^2 = -1; powers of i cycle every 4; add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers; multiply by the conjugate to divide; negative discriminant gives complex conjugate solutions; properties of rational and irrational sums and products
lessons.key_vocabulary: imaginary unit, complex number, real part, imaginary part, complex conjugate, rational, irrational
lessons.common_misconceptions: Computes (3 + 2i)(1 - i) as 3 - 2i^2 by multiplying only first and last terms; simplifies i^2 as 1 instead of -1; claims sqrt(-4) x sqrt(-9) = sqrt(36) = 6 instead of (2i)(3i) = -6
lessons.real_world_hook: Electrical engineers use complex numbers to represent alternating-current impedance; on the ACT you just need the arithmetic

lessons.learning_objective: Compute probabilities of single and compound events, use the addition and multiplication rules, and find conditional probabilities from tables
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Statistics & Probability / S-CP.A.1, S-CP.A.2, S-CP.B.7
lessons.key_concepts: P = favorable/total for equally likely outcomes; sample spaces and tree diagrams; complement P(not A) = 1 - P(A); P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B); independent events multiply; without replacement changes the second denominator; conditional probability from two-way tables uses the row or column total as the denominator; expected value
lessons.key_vocabulary: probability, sample space, complement, independent, mutually exclusive, conditional probability, without replacement, expected value
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses the grand total instead of the 'given' group's total as the denominator for a conditional probability; draws two cards without replacement but keeps the denominator the same for the second draw
lessons.real_world_hook: From a table of 200 students by grade and lunch choice, find the probability a randomly chosen junior buys lunch

lessons.learning_objective: Use the fundamental counting principle, permutations, and combinations to count outcomes and compute probabilities
lessons.key_concepts: Fundamental counting principle (multiply choices at each stage); permutations when order matters nPr = n!/(n - r)!; combinations when order does not nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!); restrictions (a digit cannot repeat, first letter must be a vowel); using counts as numerator and denominator in probability
lessons.key_vocabulary: fundamental counting principle, factorial, permutation, combination, order matters, arrangement, selection
lessons.common_misconceptions: Uses a permutation to count how many 3-person committees can be chosen from 10 people, counting the same committee 6 times; adds the number of choices at each stage instead of multiplying
lessons.real_world_hook: How many different license plates have 3 letters followed by 4 digits?

lessons.lesson_title: Statistics: distributions, data collection, and scatterplots
lessons.learning_objective: Interpret center and spread, compare distributions, evaluate data collection methods, and use scatterplots and lines of fit
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Statistics & Probability / S-ID.A.2, S-ID.B.6, S-IC.B.3
lessons.key_concepts: Mean vs median for skewed data; range, interquartile range, and standard deviation as spread; reading histograms, box plots, and stem-and-leaf plots; random sampling and bias; surveys vs experiments vs observational studies; scatterplots, positive and negative association, line of best fit and predicting with it; correlation is not causation
lessons.prerequisites: Averages, medians, and weighted means; linear functions
lessons.key_vocabulary: distribution, skew, standard deviation, interquartile range, box plot, random sample, bias, scatterplot, line of best fit, correlation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Concludes the data set with the larger range must have the larger standard deviation in every case; reads a box plot's box as containing half the data values above the median rather than the middle 50%; concludes a survey of people at a gym represents the whole town
lessons.real_world_hook: Using a scatterplot of hours studied vs ACT score to predict a score, then explaining why the prediction is uncertain

lessons.learning_objective: Add, subtract, and multiply matrices, find a 2x2 determinant, represent systems with matrices, and perform basic vector operations
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Number & Quantity / N-VM.C.6, N-VM.C.8, N-VM.C.10, N-VM.A.1
lessons.key_concepts: The ACT lists vectors and matrices in Number & Quantity and systems 'represented by simple matrices' in Algebra, topics the SAT does not test; matrix dimensions are rows x columns; add and subtract entry by entry with matching dimensions; multiplication AB requires columns of A = rows of B and gives rows of A x columns of B; row-by-column products; scalar multiplication; 2x2 determinant ad - bc; vectors as components, vector addition, magnitude sqrt(x^2 + y^2)
lessons.prerequisites: Systems of equations, arithmetic with integers
lessons.key_vocabulary: matrix, dimensions, entry, scalar, matrix product, determinant, vector, component, magnitude
lessons.common_misconceptions: Multiplies matrices entry by entry like addition; says a 2x3 matrix times a 2x3 matrix is defined; computes a determinant as ad + bc
lessons.real_world_hook: A store's price matrix times a quantity matrix gives the total revenue for each day of a weekend sale

lessons.learning_objective: Convert between exponential and logarithmic form, evaluate logarithms, apply log properties, and solve simple exponential equations
lessons.key_concepts: The ACT lists logarithmic functions in its Functions category, while the SAT does not test logarithms; log_b(x) = y means b^y = x; log_b(1) = 0 and log_b(b) = 1; product, quotient, and power rules; change of base log_b(x) = log(x)/log(b) for calculator use; solving 3^x = 20 by taking logs; common log (base 10) and natural log ln (base e); graph of y = log_b(x) as the inverse of y = b^x
lessons.prerequisites: Exponent rules, exponential functions, inverse functions
lessons.key_vocabulary: logarithm, base, argument, common log, natural log, change of base, inverse function
lessons.common_misconceptions: Rewrites log(x + y) as log x + log y; reads log_2(8) = x as 8^2 = x instead of 2^x = 8; divides log 20 by 3 instead of log 3 when solving 3^x = 20
lessons.real_world_hook: The pH scale and the decibel scale are logarithmic: a sound 10 dB louder has 10 times the intensity

lessons.learning_objective: Identify and analyze equations of circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas, and work with arithmetic and geometric sequences
lessons.ccss_code: ACT PHM: Geometry and Algebra / G-GPE.A.1, G-GPE.A.3, F-BF.A.2
lessons.key_concepts: The ACT lists 'equations of conic sections' under Geometry; circle (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2; parabola y = a(x - h)^2 + k opening up or down; ellipse (x - h)^2/a^2 + (y - k)^2/b^2 = 1 with center (h, k) and axis lengths 2a and 2b; hyperbola with a minus sign between the squared terms; recognizing the conic from its equation; arithmetic sequences a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d and geometric sequences a_n = a_1 r^(n - 1); finding a term or common difference or ratio
lessons.prerequisites: Circle equations, quadratic functions, completing the square
lessons.key_vocabulary: conic section, circle, parabola, ellipse, hyperbola, major axis, minor axis, vertex, arithmetic sequence, geometric sequence, common difference, common ratio
lessons.common_misconceptions: Reads the horizontal axis length of x^2/16 + y^2/9 = 1 as 16 instead of 2(4) = 8; uses a_1 + nd instead of a_1 + (n - 1)d for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence
lessons.real_world_hook: Satellite dishes are parabolic and planetary orbits are elliptical; whispering galleries use the ellipse's reflective property

lessons.learning_objective: Build, interpret, and evaluate mathematical models in context, and apply all course skills under timed conditions
lessons.key_concepts: ACT Modeling questions ask you to produce, interpret, understand, evaluate, and improve models, and these questions also count in other reporting categories; translating a scenario into an equation, function, or diagram; interpreting parameters (slope, intercept, growth factor) in context; checking units and reasonableness; recognizing when a model's assumptions break down; timed mixed-practice sets with error analysis afterward
lessons.key_vocabulary: model, parameter, assumption, interpret, context, reasonableness, error analysis
lessons.common_misconceptions: Interprets the y-intercept of a model as meaningful even when x = 0 is outside the data range (for example, the weight of a 0-inch-tall person); picks a linear model for data that grows by a constant percent
lessons.real_world_hook: A city's population table is used to decide whether a linear or exponential model better predicts the number of students in 10 years

lessons.lesson_title: Exponents, radicals, and rational vs irrational numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Simplify expressions with integer and rational exponents and radicals, and explain why sums and products of rational and irrational numbers are rational or irrational
lessons.key_concepts: Product, quotient, and power of a power rules; zero and negative exponents; x^(1/2) = sqrt x and x^(1/3) = cube root of x; simplifying square roots by pulling out perfect squares; rational + rational is rational, rational + irrational is irrational, nonzero rational x irrational is irrational
lessons.key_vocabulary: exponent, base, rational exponent, radical, perfect square, rational number, irrational number
lessons.common_misconceptions: Simplifies (x^3)^4 as x^7 by adding exponents; writes 2^-3 as -8 instead of 1/8; claims sqrt2 x sqrt2 being rational means the product of two irrationals is always rational
